text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Communist Party Secretary-General Do Muoi has applauded military exchanges between Vietnam and Laos during a meeting this week with a Lao People's Army delegation.
-- Industrial growth for all of 1996 could hit 14 percent, but state sector growth continues to be hampered by backward technology and a shortage of development capital.
-- Flood waters in southern Vietnam's Mekong Delta have risen to alarming levels and are expected to rise further.

-- Vietnam's Foreign Minister Nguyen Manh Cam has had talks in Washington with his American counterpart Warren Christopher and national security Advisor Anthony Lake on improving economic and trade relations.

-- Deputy Prime Minister Tran Duc Luong has told visiting Vietnam-Japan Economic Cooperation Commission chairman Akioa Nishio that Hanoi will create favourable conditions to boost economic cooperation between the two countries.
-- More than 440 cases involving drug trafficking were discovered in the first 22 days of an anti-drugs campaign launched in September. - - - -
-- A thousand households in the southern provinces of Dong Thap and An Giang have been evacuated because of dangers from flooding.
-- Ho Si Thoang of state-owned oil firm Petrovietnam has said annual gas output will reach 6.5-7 billion cubic metres after 1998. He said current gas output is 300 million cubic metres.
